pr_title: Fix incorrect MQTT Light brightness scaling using mapped bucket values instead

## Breaking change
<!--

## Proposed change

The problem pertains to inconsistencies in brightness scaling between MQTT Light and HASS. Specifically, HASS operates on a 1-255 brightness scale, while systems like Z2M use a 1-254 scale. This discrepancy leads to mismatched values; for instance, setting a brightness of 204 in HASS results in a corresponding MQTT attribute reading of 203 due to the loss of one value after surpassing half of the range.

To address this, I explored various scaling methods, noting that the primary challenges arise in the conversion from MQTT to HASS, where certain ranges correspond to multiple values for the same actual device brightness level. Consequently, I have implemented a cached mapping that aligns device values with HASS values. This ensures that any value transmitted to the device consistently corresponds to the same HASS value.

@aurimasniekis Here is a less complex solution https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/104510/files
But it fixes some rounding errors. Not perfect either.

>HASS operates on a 1-255 brightness scale, while systems like Z2M use a 1-254 scale. This discrepancy leads to mismatched values; for instance, setting a brightness of 204 in HASS results in a corresponding MQTT attribute reading of 203 due to the loss of one value after surpassing half of the range.

The reason this happens is that Home Assistant scales the brightness differently when sending and receiving brightness, which is a bug.
When sending brightness, Home Assistant *rounds* the scaled value:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/595663778cfe971ba4f15a3da584cc3d401a1531/homeassistant/components/mqtt/light/schema_json.py#L597-L601

When receiving brighness, Home Assistant *truncates* the scaled value:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/595663778cfe971ba4f15a3da584cc3d401a1531/homeassistant/components/mqtt/light/schema_json.py#L371-L375

By rounding in one direction but truncating in the other, an off-by-one error is introduce for Home Assistant brightness values of 128..254.

Building a lookup-table with scale values as proposed in this PR is not needed, we just need to correct the scaling.
Keeping track of the sent brightness, as also proposed by this PR is over complicating things.

By instead rounding the brightness in both directions, the only issue is that Home Assistant brightness value of 127 will be interpreted as 128 after the round trip; this is unavoidable since Home Assistant brightness 127 and 128 will both be scaled to Z2M brightness 127.
I'm closing this in favor of #104510

issue_context.title: Incorrect Scaling of Brightness Values in MQTT Schema JSON Light Entity
issue_context.body:
### The problem

## Description:
There's a discrepancy in the scaling of brightness values between Home Assistant (HASS) and MQTT for the MQTT Schema JSON light entity. The scaling conversion when sending brightness values from HASS to MQTT is correct. However, when receiving brightness values back from MQTT, the scaling conversion does not correctly map back to the expected range in HASS.

##  Steps to Reproduce:
* Set the brightness in HASS which triggers a scaling conversion for MQTT. For example, setting a brightness of 204 in HASS gets correctly scaled and sent as 203 to MQTT (using the conversion 204 / 255 * 254 = 203).
* When MQTT sends back a brightness value of 203, HASS incorrectly scales it, resulting in the same value of 203 instead of the expected 204.

## Expected Behavior:
The brightness value received from MQTT should be correctly scaled back to its equivalent in the HASS range. In the given example, a value of 203 received from MQTT should be converted back to 204 in HASS.

## Actual Behavior:
The scaling conversion in HASS incorrectly rounds down the value. The current conversion formula used is int(203 / float(254) * 255), which results in 203 instead of 204.

## Suggested Fix:
Modify the scaling conversion formula to include a rounding step for more accurate results. For instance, using int(round(203 / float(254), 2) * 255) would correctly produce 204.

## Code Reference:

MQTT to HASS:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mqtt/light/schema_json.py#L370-L374

HASS to MQTT:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mqtt/light/schema_json.py#L593-L601

It's advisable to conduct tests to verify the bidirectional functionality between A and B. Typically, the problems emerge when translating from B to A. This occurs if multiple A values correspond to a single B value, resulting in inconsistencies when reading back from the device. For instance, consider B = 50 mapping to A values of 127, 128, and 129. If you set the device to 127 but read back 129, it demonstrates this issue. To mitigate this, I implemented a dictionary to map these values and track the last sent request. In this example, it means storing 127 as equivalent to 50. While this approach may not be perfect, it should address most cases effectively.
